model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира зависимостта на перплекситета от спарситетния дял при две различни модели, означени като Per-Output и Per-Layer, като се използва стълбовидна диаграма с логаритмична скала по вертикалната ос. Хоризонталната ос представлява спарситетния дял, измерен в проценти, и включва стойности от 10% до 80% с интервали от 10%. Вертикалната ос, означена като Perplexity, показва перплекситета и е изградена по логаритмична скала, със стойности от 1 до 1000, като основните маркировки са на 10⁰, 10¹ и 10². Всяка стойност по хоризонталната ос съответства на група от два стълба – синият, представящ Per-Output, и оранжевият, представящ Per-Layer – които са разположени близо до един друг, като стълбовете са подредени по низходящ ред спрямо спарситетния дял. Всеки стълб отговаря на определена стойност на спарситетния дял, като визуално се наблюдава, че и двете стойности на перплекситета нарастват с увеличаване на спарситетния дял, като стълбовете за Per-Layer са по-високи от тези за Per-Output при всички дадени стойности на спарситетния дял.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical y-axis represents perplexity, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000), with major gridlines and tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, and 10². For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed side-by-side: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. The bars are generally low for sparsity rates of 10% to 40%, with Per-Output (blue) consistently showing a slightly lower perplexity than Per-Layer (orange). At 50% sparsity, both models show a perceptible increase in perplexity, with the orange bar being slightly higher. At 60% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases further, with the orange bar again being higher than the blue bar. At 70% sparsity, both models show a significant jump in perplexity, with the orange bar reaching a value of approximately 10² (100) and the blue bar reaching approximately 10¹ (10). At 80% sparsity, both models exhibit the highest perplexity values on the chart, with the orange bar reaching a value of approximately 10³ (1000) and the blue bar reaching a value of approximately 10² (100). The chart includes a legend in the top-left corner that identifies the blue bars as "Per-Output" and the orange bars as "Per-Layer". The bars are not sorted by height, and there are no visual emphases such as shading or outlines on any of the bars.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity of two models, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across various sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with values increasing from left to right, while the y-axis shows perplexity on a logarithmic scale, spanning from $10^0$ (1) to $10^3$ (1000). For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed: a blue bar for "Per-Output" and an orange bar for "Per-Layer." The data shows that both models exhibit increasing perplexity as the sparsity rate increases. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 40%), the perplexity for both models is low and relatively similar, with values around 1. As the sparsity rate increases to 50%, the perplexity for both models rises to approximately 2. At 60% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases further to about 4. At 70% sparsity, the perplexity for "Per-Output" is approximately 15, while for "Per-Layer" it is around 40. At the highest sparsity rate of 80%, the perplexity for "Per-Output" is approximately 600, and for "Per-Layer" it is approximately 1000. The chart clearly indicates that "Per-Layer" consistently has a higher perplexity than "Per-Output" at each sparsity level, and the gap between them widens significantly as sparsity increases.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt die Perplexität in Abhängigkeit von der Sparsitätsrate für zwei verschiedene Modelle, „Per-Output“ und „Per-Layer“, wobei die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala dargestellt ist. Die horizontale Achse repräsentiert die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent, mit Werten von 10% bis 80% in 10%-Schritten, und die vertikale Achse stellt die Perplexität in einem logarithmischen Maßstab dar, der von 10⁰ bis 10³ reicht. Für jede Sparsitätsrate sind zwei Balken gruppiert: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output“ und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer“. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Sparsitätsrate aufsteigend angeordnet. Die Höhe der Balken variiert mit der Sparsitätsrate, wobei für die Sparsitätsrate von 80% der höchste Wert für die Perplexität beobachtet wird, sowohl für „Per-Output“ als auch für „Per-Layer“. Die Legende oben links identifiziert die beiden Modelle durch Farbe. Die Balken sind nicht hervorgehoben, sondern unterscheiden sich lediglich durch ihre Farbe.
